title: Circular (ramp entry): stay at depth between levels instead of retracting to the clearance height and rapiding back to the cut floor

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
What happens: a Circular operation with entry Ramp (helical, after PR #1663) retracts to the clearance height after every depth level, then rapids straight back down to the floor it just cut, then starts the next helix. Seen in a PathPilot Hub run on the 770MX simulator, 2026-11-14 (file `hub-tests/1663-circular-ramp/pr.nc`, PR head 8d63209a; T4 4 mm end mill; 6 mm hole, two rings r 0.0394 and r 0.0197; steps 0.0394 in):

```
G3 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z-0.0987 I0.0394 J0 F19.69   (last ring of the level)
G0 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z0.1969                       (rapid up to clearance)
G0 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z-0.0987                      (rapid down to the floor just cut)
G3 X-1.4066 Y0.1412 Z-0.1037 I-0.0394 J0 F19.69   (next helix starts)
```

It is safe: the moves are straight up and down at one X/Y inside the cut hole. But:
- Each level adds an air trip to the clearance height and back. That costs time on a deep hole with many levels.
- The rapid down ends exactly on the previous floor, with no gap. A rapid usually stops a small clearance above the floor, and the last part is fed.

Wanted: between depth levels of one Circular operation, either
- (a) stay at depth: the next helix continues from the end of the last ring with no retract (the material below is uncut, and the helix ramps into it), or
- (b) if a retract is kept, rapid down only to a small clearance above the previous floor (for example the operation's ramp clearance), then feed the rest.

(a) is preferred. A retract should stay only where the tool must leave the hole (the last level, or a level change that needs a lift). The ramp entry and the refusals stay unchanged. The posted G-code changes, so update the circular goldens with the reason.

Found while running the Hub check for PR #1663 (issue #1609).

Done means: a pin shows no rapid to the clearance height between levels of one Circular operation (or, with option b, no rapid that ends below the previous floor plus the clearance). The circular goldens are updated, and the stock simulation still shows no gouge.

body:
Part of #874. Found while working #874 (PR #1804). Related: #320, #303, #1595.

**What happens now.** The program walk (`crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs`, `walk`) takes a verdict of the stock before it leaves the walk's sight, and keeps the gouges for the final verdict (`keep_gouges`, `fold_left`):

- when a later setup takes a new block (#320);
- when the stock is turned side-on (#874, PR #1804).

That verdict is `judge`: the stock against the parts. It does not apply `credit_breaks` (#303) or `credit_marks` (#1595). The final verdict applies them only for the operations of the last setup (`program_breaks`, `program_marks` in `stock_sim.rs`).

**The risk.** A chamfer, a deburr, an Engrave or a Trace in the earlier setup cuts below the model by design. The kept verdict can count that cut as a gouge, and the post gate then refuses a correct program. This was not reproduced with a fixture; it follows from the code. The first step is a test that shows it.

**The work.** Apply the breaks and the marks of the earlier setup's operations to the verdict that `walk` takes before a new block or a side-on turn.

**Done means:** a program with a chamfer in Setup1 and a side-on (or new-block) Setup2 reads no gouge for the chamfer; a real gouge in Setup1 still reads; a pinning test for each.

title: Carry machined stock side-on exactly: remove the one-cell over-read on turned faces

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Part of #874. Found while working #874 (PR #1804). Related: #637, #589, #321.

**What happens now.** PR #1804 carries the machined stock through a side-on quarter turn with a conservative read of the column body (`Body::carry_side`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry_side.rs`). The carried stock is never smaller than the real stock. The cost is this:

- A wall that the tool flank cut, or a step, is read up to one grid cell outside the real face after the turn.
- A cavity seen from the side (a pocket of the earlier setup) is filled.
- The field engine refuses a side-on turn by name (`FIELD_SIDE_CARRY_REFUSAL`).

**What a user can see.**

- The verdict can show rest of up to one cell on a face that is finished.
- The carried-fixture law (#321, `fixture_carried.rs`) can refuse a fixture that touches a turned face that was machined. The workaround is the setup's own stock.
- Rest machining in the turned setup can cut air in a filled cavity.

**The work.** Carry the stock side-on with the wall positions the engine knows, not the column pitch. One path is the field engine: re-index its 3-D bricks through the full signed permutation (`field_turn.rs` has the lattice turns only) and give it a column read that does not assume cuts along Z (`column_span`, `cut_ups`, `cut_downs`). The decision record `docs/decisions/874-side-on-carry.md` lists what was considered.

**Rule that stays.** The carried stock is never smaller than the real stock. A turn that the engine cannot carry is refused by name.

**Done means:** a plate with a contoured wall is carried side-on and the turned wall is read within the verdict tolerance, not one cell outside; a fixture in contact with that wall is not refused; a pocket of the earlier setup is still a cavity after the turn; a pinning test checks all three, and the field engine no longer refuses the side-on turn (or the issue says why it must).

body:
What happens: CamCraft cannot post a tapered wire EDM cut. `crates/app/src/machine/wire_edm.rs` refuses a leaning wire when the machine file states no `edm.max_taper_deg`, states no guide heights (`edm.lower_guide_z`, `edm.upper_guide_z`), or when the lean passes the stated maximum. `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` refuses every non-zero taper: the post writes a vertical 2-axis cut only. No shipped path applies a taper angle to a cut.

Expected: a user sets a taper on a wire operation for a machine that can cut it, and the post applies the taper law. A parameter that looks configurable but always refuses is a misleading state.

Evidence: review of PR #1793, head ef93ed0bf, comment 6890311801 (2026-11-15). The first body of this issue cited `Machine::wire_plane_normal` in `crates/post/src/post/machine.rs`, `crates/post/src/post/wire_align.rs`, and a refusal string in `crates/app/src/post/stream.rs`. Those names do not exist in main. Comment 6889993998 (mkinney's worker) and a code grep of main confirm this. The gap stands; the mechanism was misread.

Done means: a wire operation with a non-zero taper either posts an angled path on a machine whose file states `edm.max_taper_deg` and guide heights, or the GUI refuses the taper parameter with the named diagnostic from `wire_edm.rs`. A wire stream test drives `taper_deg` non-zero through the post and pins the output.

Workaround: leave the taper at zero.

body:
**The request (the user, 2026-11-14):** "create an ai chat window in CamCraft that would interact with ai thru mcp or whatever appropriate. Make sure that we help those agents with appropriate skill stuff for various ai tools like Claude, codex, Gemini, unsloth, ollama, etc."

This is a research umbrella (`needs-research`). It answers the open questions below in comments. Then it files the concrete sub-issues and closes. No code goes on this issue.

## What exists today

- `camcraft-cli mcp` is an MCP server on stdio. An agent drives one headless document.
- The app can start with `--mcp-port`, and `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` bridges an external agent to the open window. The agent then drives the live document.
- The skill `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/` documents the tools for Claude Code.
- Every MCP tool calls the same undoable commands as the GUI (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool").

## Goal

1. **In-app chat panel.** A dock panel in CamCraft where the user types a request, for example "add a 2D pocket on the selected face with T3". An AI model answers and acts through the same MCP tool set. The panel shows each tool call and its result.
2. **Provider choice.** The user picks the model provider and the model:
   - **Cloud:** Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT/Codex models), Google (Gemini).
   - **Local:** Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp server (most local servers have an OpenAI-compatible API).
3. **External agents.** Each external agent tool gets one documented way to drive the open app (`--mcp-port` plus `mcp --connect`), and a skill or instruction file in its own format:
   - Claude Code: `.claude/skills/` (exists; keep it current);
   - Codex CLI: AGENTS.md section or `.codex/` instructions;
   - Gemini / Antigravity CLI: `GEMINI.md` and `.agents/skills/`;
   - local models through Ollama or Unsloth: a short system prompt plus the tool list.

## Open questions (answer each in a comment)

1. **Panel architecture.** In-process, where the app calls the provider API and maps the MCP tools to the provider's tool-calling format? Or a separate process that speaks MCP to the app? What keeps the UI thread free (async, cancel)?
2. **One tool schema for all providers.** Map the MCP tool schemas to the Anthropic Messages tool format, the OpenAI tools format, and Gemini function declarations. Which local models do tool calling well enough? What is the fallback for a model without tool calling?
3. **Safety.**
   - Every action goes through the undoable commands.
   - The chat never posts G-code, never writes a file, and never changes a machine without a confirmation in the panel.
   - Group one chat turn as one undo step, or one step per command?
   - How does the panel show what changed?
4. **Keys and privacy.**
   - Where do API keys live (the OS keychain)?
   - What is sent to a cloud model (the project data, the model geometry)?
   - How does an offline-only setting work (local models only)?
5. **Context size.** How does a large project (many operations, big meshes) fit a model's context window? Summaries, on-demand tool reads?
6. **Skills per tool.** One source of truth for the tool docs (generated from the MCP tool list?) with per-tool wrappers, so the docs never drift from the shipped tools.
7. **Tests.** Test the panel and the tool mapping without network access (a scripted fake provider).
8. **Clean room.** Only public API documentation of each provider and the MCP specification. No code or prompts copied from other CAM products.

## Sub-issues to file (when the research is done)

body:
`site/content/guide/operations.md` covers every operation kind in about 800 words. Give each kind its own reference page (or one section per kind on a page per group), so a user can look up the operation they're about to use.

Each page or section should give:
- what the operation is for and when to choose it over a neighbour (for example, adaptive vs pocket);
- the parameters that matter most, by tab, with their units and sensible starting values;
- the geometry it takes (which picks: faces, edges, chains, holes) and what a click picks;
- a picture of a typical toolpath;
- the refusals a user is most likely to hit, and the fix for each (link the troubleshooting page, #1244).

Groups, one page each (or one page with sections):
- 2D: facing, contour, pocket, slot, trochoidal, chamfer, engrave, trace, deburr
- 3D: adaptive, parallel, scallop, pencil, contour, and the rest of the 3D finishing set
- Holes: drill cycles, bore, thread milling, tap
- Multi-axis: rotary, swarf, flow, multi-axis contour and roughing
- Turning: facing, profiling, grooving, threading, boring, live tooling
- Probing
- Plasma
- EDM: wire and sinker (once those ship)

Only a real side-on turn between the setups is refused.

**The work:** carry the machined stock through any rigid turn between setups (at least the side-on quarter turns about X and Y - the common "machine the edge" re-clamp), once the carried body lives on the field engine (#637), with the verdicts proven exact enough and the named refusal kept for anything the engine still cannot carry.

**Done means:** Setup1 flat, Setup2 turned 90° about X (or Y) with "What Setup1 leaves behind" simulates, judges gouges and feeds rest/judged stock from the carried body; a pinning test carries a faced plate side-on and checks its volume and verdict.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
